questions.prompt: Which two lifecycle methods does `IHostedService` define?
options: `StartAsync(CancellationToken)`, which runs when the app starts, and `StopAsync(CancellationToken)`, which runs during graceful shutdown
`ExecuteAsync` and `DisposeAsync`
`Main` and `RunAsync`
`OnStart` and `OnTick`
questions.explanation: A hosted service is any class implementing `IHostedService`, which defines `StartAsync` (app start) and `StopAsync` (graceful shutdown). It is registered with `AddHostedService<T>()`.

questions.prompt: When is `BackgroundService` the better choice than implementing `IHostedService` directly?
options: When you need a custom lifecycle with manual `StartAsync` and `StopAsync`
When the work should run only once, before the app starts
When you need a continuous loop, such as a queue consumer, that runs until shutdown; you just override `ExecuteAsync`
When the service must update the UI directly
questions.explanation: `BackgroundService` simplifies `IHostedService`: you override `ExecuteAsync` for continuous or looped work like queue processing and monitoring. `IHostedService` gives more manual control, for example timer-based jobs.

questions.prompt: In `_timer = new Timer(DoWork, null, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5));`, what do the two `TimeSpan` arguments mean?
options: `TimeSpan.Zero` is the timeout and `FromMinutes(5)` is the total run time
`TimeSpan.Zero` is the due time (start immediately) and `FromMinutes(5)` is the period between runs
Both are delays before the first run
`TimeSpan.Zero` disables the timer until `FromMinutes(5)` has passed
questions.explanation: The third argument is the due time (initial delay); `TimeSpan.Zero` starts immediately. The fourth is the period, so `DoWork` runs again every 5 minutes.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a `BackgroundService` shutdown in order.
steps: The host waits for the `ExecuteAsync` task to finish
questions.explanation: On shutdown the host cancels the stopping token, waits for the task to finish and then disposes the service, with no forced thread aborts.

options: Because `ExecuteAsync` must return within one second
Because loops are not allowed in a `BackgroundService`
Because it uses too much memory on the first iteration
Because it never honors cancellation; loop on `!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested` instead
questions.explanation: The common mistakes table says `while(true)` has no cancellation. Always honor cancellation tokens for graceful shutdown, as in `while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)`.

questions.prompt: What is the risk of doing blocking work in `StartAsync`?
options: It delays app startup
It cancels the stopping token
It registers the service twice
It disposes the service immediately
questions.explanation: The best practices say to avoid blocking in `StartAsync`, because that delays app startup.
